## Legal Moves

Treat a valid argument like a *legal move* in a game. Today we collect the
moves: eight named rules, and the traps that look like rules but are not.

You will use them on Monday, to spot rules, build proofs, and design traps of
your own.


## Warm Up

A *valid argument* is a *legal inference*. Content can change; form is what makes it valid.

- If the lab is open, I’ll go. The lab is open. **So I’ll go.** 

- If the exam is today, the forum is quiet. The forum isn’t quiet. **So the exam isn’t today.** 

---

## Micro Rule Cards {.smaller}

Given the premises, what can you infer?

:::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **MP**: from `p→q, p` infer \_\_\_\_\_\_
- **MT**: from `p→q, ¬q` infer \_\_\_\_\_\_
- **HS**: from `p→q, q→r` infer \_\_\_\_\_\_
- **DS**: from `p∨q, ¬p` infer \_\_\_\_\_\_
- **∧-Intro**: from `p, q` infer \_\_\_\_\_\_
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
- **∧-Elim**: from `p∧q` infer \_\_\_\_\_\_
- **∨-Intro**: from `p` infer \_\_\_\_\_\_
- **RES**: from `p∨q, ¬p∨r` infer \_\_\_\_\_\_
- **CD**: from `(p→r), (q→s), (p∨q)` infer \_\_\_\_\_\_
:::
::::

**Common traps:**

:::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Affirming consequent: `p→q, q ∴ p` ❌
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
- Denying antecedent: `p→q, ¬p ∴ ¬q` ❌
:::
::::

::: notes
Ask the room (Noah or Perrie) before filling each one in. The nine Rule Card
slides that follow are the reveal, one at a time, so do not rush this.

  MP        q                  MT        ~p
  HS        p->r               DS        q
  ^-Intro   p^q                ^-Elim    p  (or q)
  v-Intro   pvq  (any q)       RES       qvr
  CD        rvs

The two traps are already shown as traps -- they are the contrast, not a guess.
:::

---

## Rule Card: Modus Ponens (MP)

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p→q</code> and <code>p</code>, infer <code>q</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
If the bus is full, I’ll walk. The bus is full. **So I’ll walk.**

---

## Rule Card: Modus Tollens (MT)

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p→q</code> and <code>¬q</code>, infer <code>¬p</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
If office hours moved, Slack has an announcement. No announcement. **So they didn’t move.**

---

## Rule Card: Hypothetical Syllogism (HS)

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p→q</code> and <code>q→r</code>, infer <code>p→r</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
If tidy then joins are simpler; if simpler joins then faster viz; **so tidy ⇒ faster viz.**

---

## Rule Card: Disjunctive Syllogism (DS)

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p∨q</code> and <code>¬p</code>, infer <code>q</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
Dinner is sushi or tacos. Not sushi. **So tacos.**

---

## Rule Card: Conjunction / Simplification

<div class="two-col">
<div class="card rule">
<strong>∧-Intro</strong>: from <code>p, q</code> infer <code>p∧q</code>
</div>
<div class="card rule">
<strong>∧-Elim</strong>: from <code>p∧q</code> infer <code>p</code> (or <code>q</code>)
</div>
</div>

---

## Rule Card: ∨-Intro

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p</code> infer <code>p∨q</code>.
</div>

**Ex:** I rode my scooter today, **so I either rode my scooter or I'm a unicorn.**

**Note** validity cares about *form*, not plausibility of the added disjunct.

---

## Rule Card: Resolution (RES)

<div class="card rule">
From <code>p∨q</code> and <code>¬p∨r</code> infer <code>q∨r</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
Either study or soccer; if study then library. **So soccer or library.**

---

## Rule Card: Constructive Dilemma (CD)

<div class="card rule">
From <code>(p→r), (q→s), (p∨q)</code> infer <code>r∨s</code>.
</div>

**Ex:**  
If sunny then picnic; if rainy then museum; sunny or rainy; **so picnic or museum.**

---

## Fallacy Cards (flash)

<div class="two-col">
<div class="card rule">
<strong>Affirming the consequent</strong> ❌  
<code>from p→q, q infer p</code>
</div>
<div class="card rule">
<strong>Denying the antecedent</strong> ❌  
<code>from p→q, ¬p infer ¬q</code>
</div>
</div>

## Validity

**∧-Elim**: $(p\wedge q)\rightarrow p$ is this always true?


## INValidity

**Affirming Consequent**: $((p\rightarrow q)\wedge q)\rightarrow p$ is this always true?


| $p$ | $q$ | $p\rightarrow q$ | $(p\rightarrow q)\wedge q$ | $((p\rightarrow q)\wedge q)\rightarrow p$ |
|---|---|:--------:|:--------:|:--------:|
| F | F |       |      |      |      
| F | T |       |       |       |       
| T | F |       |       |       |       
| T | T |       |       |       |
